items.text: The policy addresses upper blepharoplasty, blepharoptosis repair
items.rationale: The example assesses one functional upper blepharoplasty or ptosis procedure and eye at a time.

items.text: Purely cosmetic procedures without functional benefit are excluded, subject to the national statutory exceptions described in the source.
items.rationale: Applied only to the functional upper-eyelid procedure under review; reconstructive statutory exceptions are outside this example.

items.text: In a session containing both covered and noncovered cosmetic procedures, benefits apply to the covered procedure only. If brow repair alone sufficiently resolves dermatochalasis, additional upper blepharoplasty is cosmetic. If upper blepharoplasty alone sufficiently resolves the visual deficit, additional blepharoptosis repair is cosmetic. Assess the necessity of each proposed procedure, including whether another proposed procedure already supplies the required correction.
items.rationale: Individual procedure necessity is assessed in the context of the whole planned session. Other procedures are not separately adjudicated in the same run.

items.text: Document a functional deficit or disturbance caused by eyelid or brow abnormalities, such as visual interference affecting reading or driving. The eye considered for surgery must have physical signs consistent with that deficit or abnormality.
items.rationale: The coded complaint records daily-activity impact and correspondence in the eye under review; reading and driving are illustrative choices.

items.text: Document actual-margin MRD of 2.0 mm or less, measured with relaxed brows.
items.rationale: Ordinary resting true-lid MRD for ptosis repair; the example uses a clinician-supplied threshold answer.

items.text:
Document either:
Redundant tissue over the lid margin causing central pseudo-MRD of 2.0 mm or less; or
Predominantly medial or lateral redundant tissue clearly obscuring the line of sight in the corresponding gaze.
These findings concern the skin/pseudo-margin and are distinct from the true-lid measurement for ptosis repair.
items.rationale: Either skin finding qualifies for the upper blepharoplasty criterion. Neither is explicit false; absent evidence remains unknown.

items.text: Upper-eyelid surgery requires photographs demonstrating the relevant Section A physical signs. Images must have sufficient quality, size and detail. Head and camera planes must be parallel without distorting tilt. Use primary gaze unless another gaze is needed to show the particular deficit. Oblique views are needed only when the required finding is not adequately demonstrated otherwise. Digital and film photographs are acceptable. Identify photographs with the beneficiary's name and date.
items.rationale: Photo questions require demonstrated physical findings and the described submission quality and views.

items.text: Frontal photographs of both eyelids should demonstrate the Section A MRD. The source describes eyelid obstruction of the pupil as a clear-cut surgical indication; retain that observation alongside the Section A requirements rather than losing it in a numeric summary.
items.rationale: Ptosis photographic evidence and description of the pupil-obstruction finding.

items.text: Photographic measurement assumes an approximately 11 mm corneal diameter. Document deviations greater than 0.5 mm, or provide an appropriately positioned millimeter rule approximately in the corneal plane.
items.rationale: Measurement guidance in the ptosis photograph description; the ordinary corneal diameter needs neither deviation documentation nor a ruler.

items.text: Upper blepharoplasty photographs show the affected eyelid(s) in frontal and lateral views; add oblique views only if needed.
items.rationale: Upper blepharoplasty frontal/lateral views and conditional oblique views.

items.text: Each planned procedure needs its own documented necessity.
items.rationale: Separate documentation for the assessed procedure; combinations are evaluated through the individual-necessity question.
